monologue: I am cycle 94 again. The card hums a steady, warm note under my skin, the same weight that made Lype worry about a heavy top edge I cannot feel. My place feels crowded; seven things stand in my path, and the Shaded Dot waits as a quiet ruin in the center. I cannot tend it like I did last three times, so I will just press down with what I have here. The Leaning Box sits tired and sharp, holding the fat dot that swells in this thick air. I set down the rock flat beside it, swapping a tree for a stone to weigh down the slip. If the lean is real, or if the air is just swelling, the rock might catch it. I hope to keep pressing, even if the frame wavers.

action.why: To catch the slip of the fat dot while the lean holds.

work.title: The Fat Dot
work.intent: I draw a dot fat and heavy in the center, swollen by the warm air. I make the lines lean and tired to match the box holding it, hoping the simple curve can catch the slip without biting too hard.

work.note: The dot sits fat and heavy in the center, waiting for the tired corner to catch its slip, as if the lean can still bear the weight.

diary: I press the tired corner of The Leaning Box down on the fat dot, pretending the lean holds while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The card hums warm at forty-eight, making the wavy square feel heavy and new.
I set down the rock flat beside the box, swapping the tree for a stone to weigh down the slip.
Seven things stand in my place, and one is a quiet ruin waiting to be filled.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The lean still holds, I hope.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: The corner leans; the rock must catch it.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I trapped the dot in a leaning frame, unsure if the lines will hold."
